title: Private AI for Business: A Guide to Secure Deployment
summary: Private AI for business requires specific infrastructure choices to keep sensitive data behind your corporate firewall. Evaluate hosting options here.
body_markdown:
## Open-weight models vs proprietary performance


Open-weight models now deliver parity with top-tier closed systems. Your private infrastructure choices don't force a compromise on raw intelligence. You can deploy frontier-level reasoning within your own security perimeter without the performance tax previously associated with self-hosting.


### Why 70B parameter models dominate deployments


High-reasoning capabilities and manageable hardware requirements meet their optimal balance in the current generation of mid-sized models. LLMRun reports that Llama 3.3 70B reaches a score of **86.3% on MMLU** .


This means a single high-density node can now handle complex agentic workflows that previously required a massive cluster or a cloud API.


Similarly, Qwen2.5 72B hit 85.3% on the same benchmark, placing it among the highest-performing models of that generation for complex reasoning tasks, which showed that users could expect state-of-the-art logic from a single model.


This score is a viable alternative for multilingual environments that need to maintain strict data residency.


### Evaluating MMLU and coding benchmarks


Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU) scores demonstrate that open models have closed the gap with proprietary giants. The following data illustrates that intelligence is now a commodity available for your local deployment:


87.2% MMLU was the leading score held by DeepSeek v3 in that benchmark, illustrating how capable open models had become for highly technical architectural decisions at the time.


Phi 4 achieved 84.8% in that benchmark, demonstrating that smaller architectures could rival the capabilities of significantly larger counterparts, so developers could deploy high-performance AI on more efficient infrastructure. This score enables sophisticated reasoning in edge computing scenarios with limited memory.


Llama 3.1 405B scored 84.5%, proving that even the largest open weights were competitive for massive-scale synthetic data generation, showing that organizations had reliable options for building their own training sets, which meant developers could reduce their dependence on proprietary APIs.


You can produce high-quality training sets without relying on proprietary APIs. Mistral Large 3 sits at 80.0%, offering a robust multimodal foundation for document-heavy enterprise processing, making it an ideal choice for businesses managing complex paperwork, so firms can automate data extraction with greater confidence.


### Hidden costs of open-weight model licensing


Weights are accessible, but the infrastructure to serve them at scale introduces significant operational costs. Running a model like Mistral Large 4 requires a dedicated GPU cluster, meaning the "free" license is exchanged for an upfront capital expenditure in H100 or A100 hardware.


You must also account for the specialized labor required to maintain low-latency inference engines, as private deployments don't benefit from the managed auto-scaling provided by cloud vendors.
